title: Topological edge states in twisted bilayer MoS2
question: Can we engineer a flat band with non-trivial Chern number in twisted MoS2 by tuning the dielectric environment?
background: Recent experiments on twisted bilayer graphene revealed correlated insulating states and superconductivity. MoS2 is an emerging 2D semiconductor with strong spin-orbit coupling; whether the same magic-angle paradigm holds in a direct-gap system is an open question.
significance: A confirmed topological flat band in MoS2 would open a new materials platform for fault-tolerant quantum devices and strongly correlated phases at temperatures above 4K.
pathway: Fabricate twisted MoS2 bilayers at 1-3 degrees, measure transport and STM spectroscopy under tunable gating, and compare band structure to a 4-band continuum model with dielectric-screened Coulomb interactions.

title: Quantum metric drag in non-Hermitian Rice-Mele chains
question: Can a non-Hermitian dissipation term induce a measurable quantum metric drag between bands?
background: Quantum geometry is a unifying language for polarization, orbital magnetism, and nonlinear response. The recent quantum-metric drag proposal predicts a cross-band contribution that is gauge-invariant and survives 1D time-reversal symmetry.
significance: Establishing quantum metric drag experimentally would validate a new geometric transport mechanism and refine the theory of nonlinear response in open quantum systems.
pathway: Construct a dissipative Rice-Mele chain via superconducting qubit arrays, drive parametric oscillations, and read out the drag coefficient from second-harmonic current response at fixed chemical potential.

title: Magic state distillation with biased noise
question: Can we distill magic states at a higher rate by exploiting noise bias in the physical qubits?
background: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires magic states; current distillation protocols assume depolarizing noise. Real hardware exhibits biased noise channels.
significance: Lower magic-state overhead translates directly to fewer physical qubits for the same logical depth, reducing hardware cost by an order of magnitude in surface-code architectures.
pathway: Use the biased-noise Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill code as a base, design a tailored distillation circuit, and benchmark on a 2D Rydberg atom array simulator.

title: Anomaly inflow on the 5D boundary of a 4D topological superconductor
question: Does a 4D time-reversal-breaking topological superconductor host a 3D chiral conformal boundary that matches the global anomaly?
background: The 4D quantum Hall effect is a mathematical extension; its physical realization requires engineered meta-materials or synthetic dimensions. Anomaly inflow constrains the boundary.
significance: A direct observation of the boundary mode would constitute a tabletop test of anomaly inflow and chart a course for higher-dimensional topological phases in cold-atom platforms.
pathway: Construct a synthetic 4D band structure in a 1D modulated optical lattice using dimension-reduction protocols and probe the surface spectral function via momentum-resolved RF spectroscopy.

title: Replay-coupled dendritic spikes in CA1 during quiet wakefulness
question: Are dendritic Ca2+ spikes during quiet wakefulness causally linked to sharp-wave ripples in CA1?
background: Hippocampal replay during slow-wave sleep supports memory consolidation. Recent two-photon recordings show dendritic spikes in CA1 during quiet wake, but their coupling to ripples is unclear.
significance: Establishing this link would reframe dendritic spikes as a daytime rehearsal mechanism, with implications for memory therapeutics in aging and Alzheimer's disease.
pathway: Combine juxtacellular recording with two-photon Ca2+ imaging in awake mice, optogenetically suppress dendritic spikes, and quantify the effect on ripple-locked replay content.

title: Mitochondrial fission as a metabolic switch in CD8+ T cell exhaustion
question: Can we rescue exhausted tumor-infiltrating T cells by pharmacologically tuning mitochondrial fission?
background: T cell exhaustion limits checkpoint-blockade efficacy. Mitochondrial morphology is increasingly recognized as a metabolic marker of T cell fate, but causality is debated.
significance: A drug-repurposing strategy targeting Drp1 could be combined with existing checkpoint inhibitors to extend response duration in solid tumors.
pathway: Profile mitochondrial morphology in patient-derived TILs, screen a focused Drp1 modulator library, and validate top hits in a syngeneic mouse melanoma model with chronic antigen exposure.

title: Long-read single-cell chromatin accessibility in tumor microenvironments
question: Can long-read scATAC-seq resolve cell-type-specific regulatory element reuse in the tumor microenvironment?
background: Short-read scATAC-seq loses linkage between distal enhancers. Long-read protocols have been limited by throughput and barcode fidelity.
significance: Improved enhancer linkage would clarify the cis-regulatory grammar of tumor-stroma crosstalk and identify noncoding targets for synthetic-locus therapeutics.
pathway: Adapt a recently published long-read scATAC protocol, optimize barcode collision rate, and benchmark against matched short-read data from the same patient samples.

title: Horizontal gene transfer as a driver of venom innovation in cone snails
question: Did horizontal transfer of toxin-precursor genes accelerate venom diversification in Conus?
background: Cone snail venoms are a textbook case of rapid molecular evolution. The contribution of HGT versus tandem duplication is unresolved.
significance: Quantifying HGT's role in venom innovation would inform bioprospecting strategies and the design of peptide-drug libraries.
pathway: Assemble chromosome-level genomes for 30 Conus species, build a phylogeny-aware HGT detection pipeline, and validate candidate transfers with synteny and expression data.

title: Equivariant message-passing for amorphous material Hamiltonians
question: Can a strictly local-frame equivariant GNN reach chemical accuracy on amorphous LiPON Hamiltonians?
background: Equivariant GNNs (e.g. DeepH) achieve low MAE on crystalline systems. Amorphous materials break global symmetries; whether a local-frame design can still exploit geometric priors is open.
significance: A practical model for amorphous Hamiltonians would accelerate electrolyte and solid-state battery design without DFT at every iteration.
pathway: Generate a 5k amorphous LiPON dataset via tight-binding pass-through, train a 3-MPNN + 1-LCMP architecture, and compare MAE on H and S blocks to a DFT-fine-tuned baseline.

title: Serverless cold-start mitigation via warm-pool pinning with ML-predicted load
question: Can a lightweight load-prediction model cut cold-start latency by 50% over a static warm pool?
background: Serverless platforms suffer tail-latency penalties on cold start. Static warm pools waste resources during low-traffic windows.
significance: A drop-in mitigation strategy for Function-as-a-Service providers would translate directly to lower p99 latency and higher throughput-per-dollar.
pathway: Train a 1D-CNN on CloudWatch traces from a representative Lambda workload, integrate the predictor with the warm-pool controller, and benchmark p50/p99 over a 7-day production trace replay.

title: Sub-quadratic attention with spectrum-preserving random projections
question: Can a random-feature kernel approximation of attention recover transformer expressivity in O(n log n) time?
background: Linear attention is fast but loses the spectrum of the softmax kernel. Random-feature methods (RFF, ORFF) approximate the kernel but degrade on long-context reasoning.
significance: A spectrum-preserving sub-quadratic attention would enable million-token context windows on commodity GPUs, with clear impact on long-document RAG and code understanding.
pathway: Analyze the spectrum gap of ORFF approximations, design a learnable projection matrix, and benchmark against FlashAttention-2 on LongBench and SCROLLS.

title: Spec-first vs example-first prompt authoring for non-programmers
question: Do non-programmers produce more reliable prompts when authoring in spec-form vs example-form?
background: Prompt engineering is the new literacy, but pedagogical conventions have not converged. Spec-form prompts emphasize constraints, example-form prompts emphasize demonstrations.
significance: A clear pedagogical default would reduce trial-and-error cost in workforce prompt-literacy programs and improve downstream task reliability.
pathway: Run a 2x2 between-subjects study (spec vs example, structured vs freeform) with 60 participants on three tasks: data extraction, email drafting, code explanation.
